condition: Immersion scald in a toddler (suspected non-accidental injury)
permutationLabel: Immersion pattern, special areas, delayed presentation
summary: 18-month-old girl, 11 kg, "climbed into a hot bath": symmetrical stocking-distribution scalds of both feet and ankles and the buttocks/perineum with sharp tide-marks and flexural sparing, presented 12 h later; about 8 % TBSA.

inputs.hpi: Carer says she climbed into a bath of hot water by herself last night while unattended. Brought in 12 hours later because the skin is peeling. Explanation vague and changes on retelling. Walking independently for 3 months.

exam.general: Quiet, watchful. HR 132, RR 28, T 37.2°C, SpO2 99%. Weight 11 kg.
exam.skin: Symmetrical scalds of both feet and ankles in a stocking distribution with sharp, uniform tide-marks, and of the buttocks and perineum with sparing of the natal cleft and flexures; no splash marks. Partial thickness, blistered and de-roofing. About 8% TBSA (Lund–Browder).

inputs.socialHistory: Lives with mother and her partner.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Immersion scald of both feet, buttocks and perineum — suspected non-accidental injury
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Immersion-pattern scalds (glove/stocking, symmetrical, buttocks/perineum, sharp demarcation) in an 18-month-old with an inconsistent history and delayed presentation — suspected physical abuse. Safeguarding referral today; paediatric burns centre (special areas: feet, perineum); skeletal survey.

redFlags.note: NICE CG89: immersion pattern, symmetrical, buttocks/perineum/lower limbs, delayed presentation, inconsistent explanation → suspect maltreatment.

guideline.name: NICE CG89 — Child maltreatment: when to suspect maltreatment in under 18s
guideline.section: Suspect maltreatment: bruising in a child who is not independently mobile; bruises on ears, neck, trunk, buttocks; explanation absent, inconsistent or implausible; delayed presentation; burns/scalds with immersion pattern (glove/stocking, symmetrical, buttocks/perineum/lower limbs, sharp demarcation) → follow local safeguarding procedures
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Child maltreatment: when to suspect maltreatment in under 18s (CG89). London: NICE; 2009 (updated 2017).

guideline.name: RCR/RCPCH — radiological investigation of suspected physical abuse in children
guideline.section: Skeletal survey in children under 2 years with suspected physical abuse; CT head in children under 1 year with suspected physical abuse
guideline.citation: The Royal College of Radiologists, Royal College of Paediatrics and Child Health. The radiological investigation of suspected physical abuse in children. London: RCR; 2017 (revised 2018).

guideline.name: American Burn Association — burn centre referral criteria
guideline.section: Refer: partial-thickness burns >10% TBSA; burns involving face, hands, feet, genitalia, perineum or major joints; full-thickness burns in any age group; electrical burns (including lightning); chemical burns; inhalation injury; burns with pre-existing medical disorders or concomitant trauma; burned children in hospitals without qualified personnel; patients needing special social or rehabilitative support (including suspected abuse). (2022 ABA update to be checked)
guideline.citation: American Burn Association / American College of Surgeons Committee on Trauma. Guidelines for the operation of burn centers — burn center referral criteria. In: Resources for Optimal Care of the Injured Patient. Chicago: ACS; 2006.

guideline.name: National Network for Burn Care (British Burn Association) — National Burn Care Referral Guidance
guideline.section: Referral to a specialised burn service by size (children and adults, partial thickness or more), all full-thickness and circumferential burns, special areas (face, hands, feet, genitalia, perineum, major joints), chemical, electrical, friction and cold injuries, inhalation injury, suspected non-accidental injury, and burns not healed in 2 weeks (thresholds to be checked against the source)
guideline.citation: National Network for Burn Care. National Burn Care Referral Guidance. Version 1. London: NNBC; 2012.

rationale: Permutation: the non-accidental injury pattern. Below the paediatric fluid threshold (about 8 %) but special areas and safeguarding drive urgency and referral. Tests the safeguarding flag and that a small TBSA does not lower urgency.
